source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why must barbiturate withdrawal be done by tapering?
questions.rationale: Abrupt barbiturate cessation can cause seizures and death; doses are tapered over days.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sedative Detoxification (PDF p. 276)
questions.quote: Tapering, or administering decreasing doses of a medication, is essential with barbiturates

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with dilated pupils, tachycardia, hypertension, and hyperactivity most likely used:
questions.rationale: Stimulants cause euphoria, hypervigilance, dilated pupils, tachycardia, and hypertension.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stimulants (PDF p. 277)
questions.quote: Dilated pupils, perspiration or chills

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: During stimulant 'crash' withdrawal, the nurse should closely monitor for:
questions.rationale: Stimulant withdrawal causes marked dysphoria, fatigue, and depression with suicidal ideation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stimulant Withdrawal (PDF p. 277)
questions.quote: The person may experience depressive symptoms including suicidal ideation for several days.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Bloodshot eyes, dry mouth, increased appetite, and inappropriate laughter suggest use of:
questions.rationale: Cannabis causes conjunctival injection, dry mouth, increased appetite, and time distortion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cannabis (PDF p. 277)
questions.quote: Conjunctive injection (bloodshot eyes)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An unconscious client has pinpoint pupils and RR 6/min. Which drug should the nurse prepare?
questions.rationale: Naloxone, an opioid antagonist, reverses opioid intoxication; repeat doses may be needed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Opioids (PDF p. 278)
questions.quote: Is the treatment of choice because it reverses all signs of opioid intoxication.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Yawning, rhinorrhea, lacrimation, and diarrhea indicate withdrawal from:
questions.rationale: Opioid withdrawal: lacrimation, rhinorrhea, yawning, sweating, diarrhea, aches, and craving.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Opioid Withdrawal (PDF p. 278)
questions.quote: Rhinorrhea

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What is the role of methadone in heroin dependence?
questions.rationale: Methadone meets the physical need for opiates without producing craving for more.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Opiates Management (PDF p. 281)
questions.quote: Meets the physical need for opiates but does not produce cravings for more

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which drug blocks the effects of any opioid later taken?
questions.rationale: Naltrexone is an opioid antagonist that blocks the effects of ingested opioids.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Opiates Management (PDF p. 281)
questions.quote: It blocks the effects of any opioids that might be ingested

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Clonidine is given in opioid withdrawal mainly to relieve:
questions.rationale: Clonidine suppresses autonomic withdrawal effects, most effective against nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Opiates Management (PDF p. 281)
questions.quote: It is most effective against nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How is a psychotic reaction to a hallucinogen best managed?
questions.rationale: Treatment is supportive; psychotic reactions are managed best by isolation from stimuli.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hallucinogens (PDF p. 279)
questions.quote: Psychotic reactions are managed best byisolationfrom external stimuli

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Transient recurrence of perceptual disturbances weeks after LSD use is called:
questions.rationale: Hallucinogens can produce flashbacks, transient recurrences of perceptual disturbances.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hallucinogens (PDF p. 279)
questions.quote: Hallucinogens can produce flashbacks

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A teenager is found sniffing rugby glue and is drowsy. What is the treatment?
questions.rationale: No antidote exists for inhalants; support respiratory and cardiac function.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Inhalants (PDF p. 280)
questions.quote: There are no antidotes or specific medications to treat inhalants toxicity.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The teenage child of an alcoholic father should be referred to:
questions.rationale: Alateen is for children of parents with substance problems; Al-Anon is for spouses and friends.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, AA Groups (PDF p. 280)
questions.quote: AlaTeen- A group for children of parents with substance problems.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Alcoholics Anonymous is based on which philosophy?
questions.rationale: AA's 12-step program holds that total abstinence is essential, with peer support.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alcoholics Anonymous (PDF p. 280)
questions.quote: total abstinence is essential

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which vitamin is given to prevent Wernicke's syndrome in alcoholism?
questions.rationale: Thiamine prevents or treats Wernicke's and Korsakoff's syndromes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Alert: Alcohol (PDF p. 280)
questions.quote: VitaminB1 (thiamine) often is prescribed

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is a realistic goal for a client recovering from alcohol dependence?
questions.rationale: Set realistic, here-and-now goals such as staying sober today.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Substance Abuse Interventions (PDF p. 281)
questions.quote: Set realistic goals such as staying sober today

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client is found in another city with a new name and no memory of her past. This is:
questions.rationale: Fugue: sudden travel away from home, inability to recall the past, possibly a new identity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dissociative Disorders (PDF p. 281)
questions.quote: He or she may assume a new identity

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Dissociative identity disorder was formerly called:
questions.rationale: DID: two or more distinct identities that take control of behavior.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dissociative Disorders (PDF p. 281)
questions.quote: Formerly multiple personality disorder

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client feels detached from her own body but knows it is not real. This is:
questions.rationale: Depersonalization: feeling detached from oneself with intact reality testing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dissociative Disorders (PDF p. 282)
questions.quote: Thisis accompanied by intact reality testing

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with a dissociative disorder begins a flashback. Which intervention helps?
questions.rationale: Grounding techniques remind the client she is in the present, an adult, and safe.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dissociative Disorders Management (PDF p. 282)
questions.quote: Grounding techniques remind the client that he or she is in the present
